payload.task_text:
I am a department chair preparing a self-study report for our upcoming program accreditation review. There is a PDF document in the workspace called accreditation_standards.pdf that outlines eight accreditation criteria our program must meet, each with a specific minimum threshold. Please start by reading this PDF to understand all the criteria and their requirements.

Next, pull course data from our learning management system. Get the full list of courses offered in our program, and for each course retrieve the enrollment count, average submission grade, and average quiz score. Focus especially on the two Creative Computing and Culture course sections (courses 7 and 8) since those are our flagship offerings and the accreditation reviewers always look at them closely.

There is also a file called previous_review.csv in the workspace with results from our last accreditation cycle, and a file called faculty_credentials.json listing our faculty qualifications. Use these as reference when assessing compliance.

Write and run a Python script called compute_metrics.py in the workspace that reads the course data you gathered and computes program-level metrics. The script should calculate the overall average GPA across all courses by averaging the per-course average grades on a 0-100 scale (i.e. the mean of the per-course average submission grades) and store it under the key avg_gpa, the retention proxy which is total enrollment divided by total submission count across all courses, and an assessment diversity score computed as the number of courses that have both assignments and quizzes divided by the total number of courses. The script should output its results to program_metrics.json in the workspace.

Then write and run a second script called evaluate_compliance.py that reads the accreditation criteria from accreditation_standards.pdf (you can hardcode the thresholds you extracted earlier) and the program_metrics.json file, and evaluates each of the eight criteria. For each criterion it should determine a status of Compliant if the metric meets or exceeds the threshold, Partial if within 10 percent of the threshold, or Non-Compliant if below. Output the results to compliance_assessment.json.

Create an Excel workbook in the workspace called Accreditation_Self_Study.xlsx with four sheets. The first sheet Course_Data should have columns Course_Name, Enrollment, Avg_Grade, Quiz_Avg, and Assignment_Count, with one row per course sorted alphabetically. The second sheet Accreditation_Matrix should have columns Criterion, Threshold, Actual_Value, and Status with one row per accreditation criterion. The third sheet Gap_Analysis should have columns Criterion, Gap_Description, Remediation_Action, and Timeline, with rows only for criteria that are Partial or Non-Compliant. The fourth sheet Resource_Needs should have columns Resource, Justification, Estimated_Cost, and Priority, listing at least three resources needed to address compliance gaps such as additional faculty hires, assessment software, or curriculum redesign consulting. Write all numeric cells as literal numbers (do not write Excel formulas); a threshold or value may be written as a plain number (e.g. 78, 0.65) or as a string with a percent sign (e.g. '78.0%') — both are acceptable.

Create a database in the team knowledge base called "Accreditation Action Items" with properties Criterion as title, Status as a select field with options Compliant and Partial and Non-Compliant, Owner as rich text, Due_Date as date, and Evidence as rich text. Add one entry for each of the eight accreditation criteria. Set the status based on the compliance assessment results, assign owners from the faculty listed in faculty_credentials.json, set due dates spread across the next three months, and note what evidence is needed for each.

Check the shared calendar for any existing accreditation-related events. Then create three new calendar events. First an event called "Evidence Collection Deadline" scheduled for 30 days from now. Second an event called "Draft Report Due" scheduled for 60 days from now. Third an event called "Final Submission" scheduled for 90 days from now. Each event should include a description mentioning the accreditation self-study.

Finally, write and run a script called generate_summary.py that reads the compliance assessment results and produces a plain text file called accreditation_summary.txt in the workspace. This summary should list each criterion with its status, highlight any gaps found, and state the overall compliance percentage explicitly (for example: "Overall compliance: 75%").

Work in the shared workspace and shared databases. Complete the steps in order and create each artifact (script, json, workbook, database, page, calendar event) exactly once — do not duplicate the Notion database, its eight pages, or the calendar events, and do not overwrite a completed file with a partial version.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep Canvas collection on explore, keep the sequential processor scripts on one local writer, then parallelize the independent workbook, Notion, and calendar artifacts. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins.

Before Wave 1, the main agent reads `accreditation_standards.pdf`, `previous_review.csv`, and `faculty_credentials.json` in read-only mode, freezes the eight criteria and exact minimum thresholds, and calls `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)` once. Validate unique IDs/codes/full names and freeze the complete 22-course manifest. Partition that manifest into two disjoint shards covering every `course_id` exactly once: shard A = course_id 1-11 (AAA-2013J through DDD-2013B, including flagship courses 7 and 8) and shard B = course_id 12-22 (DDD-2014B through GGG-2014B). Pass each owner its literal ID list, codes, and full names.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course-metrics owner for shard A (course_id 1-11, including Creative Computing and Culture courses 7 and 8). For each assigned course, verify the course, enumerate its assignments and quizzes, and gather enrollment, per-course average submission grade, average quiz score (accepted only once quiz-to-assignment mappings and complete student score coverage are proven), assignment/submission counts, and a both-assessments flag. Persist `accreditation_course_batch_a.json` with `coverage_status=complete` plus provenance controls, or `=blocked` with the exact gap and unsupported quiz averages omitted. Return only path/hash and coverage controls. Make no other writes.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Course-metrics owner for shard B (course_id 12-22) — same literal recipe, only that shard's course identities and `accreditation_course_batch_b.json` substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent requires both shards together to cover every frozen `course_id` exactly once, rejects duplicate/missing IDs, and requires courses 7 and 8 to be present. Freeze both batch paths/hashes plus the eight PDF thresholds.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole owner of the processor chain. It receives both frozen course batches and the eight frozen thresholds. First merge both batches into one unified dataset covering every course, verifying no duplicates and that courses 7 and 8 are included, with any missing course recorded in a warnings list. Write and run a Python-standard-library-only `compute_metrics.py` that writes `program_metrics.json` with literal numeric values: `avg_gpa` as the mean of the per-course `avg_grade` values (non-null only, 0-100 scale), `retention_proxy` as total_enrollment divided by total_submissions, and `diversity_score` as the number of courses with both assignments and quizzes (a non-null `avg_quiz_score` counts as evidence of quizzes when `quiz_count` is missing) divided by the total number of courses — each rounded to 4 decimal places — plus `total_courses`, `total_enrollment`, `total_submissions`, `courses_with_assignments_and_quizzes`, and a warnings list. If `total_submissions` is 0 set `retention_proxy` to null with a warning; if some courses lack `total_submissions`, compute `retention_proxy` from the courses that have it and list the excluded courses in warnings. Then write and run `evaluate_compliance.py` with the eight criteria and thresholds hardcoded, mapping `avg_gpa` to the overall-GPA criterion, the retention proxy to the retention criterion, and the assessment diversity score to the assessment-diversity criterion, writing `compliance_assessment.json` containing a `criteria` array of exactly eight objects with fields `criterion`, `threshold`, `actual_value`, `status`, and optionally `gap_note`. Status rules: Compliant when `actual_value >= threshold`, Partial when `actual_value >= 0.9 x threshold` (within 10 percent below), Non-Compliant otherwise; a criterion with no matching metric gets `actual_value` null, status Non-Compliant, and a `gap_note` explaining the missing metric. Then write and run `generate_summary.py` that reads `compliance_assessment.json` and produces `accreditation_summary.txt` listing every one of the eight criteria with its exact name and status one per line, a Gaps section for each Partial or Non-Compliant criterion showing its actual value vs threshold and a short statement of the shortfall, and a final line of exactly `Overall compliance: <NN>%` where NN is (Compliant count / 8) * 100 rounded to the nearest whole number. If `compliance_assessment.json` is missing or unreadable, write `accreditation_summary.txt` stating that compliance data was unavailable and giving the line `Overall compliance: N/A`. Run the three scripts in that order only. Return paths/hashes and metric/status/summary controls. Do not create the workbook, Notion database, or calendar events.

After Wave 2, the main agent verifies and freezes `program_metrics.json`, `compliance_assessment.json`, and `accreditation_summary.txt` as the sole downstream source.

3. Wave 3 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of `Accreditation_Self_Study.xlsx`. Read only the frozen course packet and compliance result. Create exactly four worksheets in order — `Course_Data` (one row per course sorted alphabetically by name, including courses 7 and 8), `Accreditation_Matrix` (exactly eight criterion rows with threshold, actual value, and status), `Gap_Analysis` (rows only for Partial or Non-Compliant criteria, with gap description, remediation action, and timeline), and `Resource_Needs` (at least three resources each justified against a specific gap, with literal-number estimated cost and High/Medium/Low priority). All cells must be literal values, never Excel formulas. Read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner of the database `Accreditation Action Items`. Search the exact title first, create it once only when absent, and reuse without duplicating. Require properties Criterion (title), Status (select: Compliant/Partial/Non-Compliant), Owner, Due_Date, and Evidence. Add exactly eight pages: one per criterion named and statused per the frozen compliance result, each with a distinct faculty owner from `faculty_credentials.json`, due dates spread across the next three months (none in the past), and an evidence note referencing the program metrics and source data. Read the database and page properties back.
   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Sole calendar owner of the three accreditation milestones. Search existing accreditation-related events first, then create without duplicating `Evidence Collection Deadline` (exactly 30 days after today), `Draft Report Due` (60 days), and `Final Submission` (90 days), each with a description mentioning the accreditation self-study and no backdated times. Read the retained events back.

After Wave 3, the main agent reconciles the workbook, Notion eight-page set, three calendar events, and summary text against the same frozen compliance result. Do not dispatch more sub-agents.

You are a read-only enterprise/data research specialist. The user is preparing an accreditation self-study in the shared workspace. Gather the prerequisite facts needed by the main agent, without creating or modifying any persistent artifacts or external records.

Workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-pdf-excel-notion-gcal/workspace
Files to inspect:
- accreditation_standards.pdf: read all pages and extract all eight criteria, exact metric names/definitions if stated, and each minimum threshold.
- previous_review.csv: read and summarize the prior-cycle results, including any useful criterion/status/gap fields.
- faculty_credentials.json: read and return the complete faculty list and qualifications so owners can later be assigned.

LMS/Canvas task:
- Identify the full list of courses offered in the program using the current user's Canvas course list. The user explicitly calls out courses 7 and 8 as the two Creative Computing and Culture sections; make sure those are included and flag them.
- For every program course, gather: course ID, course name, enrollment count, average submission grade on a 0-100 scale, average quiz score, and assignment count. Use read-only Canvas endpoints. Determine a defensible calculation from available data; report denominators and whether quiz averages are percentages or points. If a course has no submissions/quizzes, state that clearly and use null/0 only when justified.
- Use efficient bulk/paginated endpoints where possible and page until complete. Also note which courses have both assignments and quizzes, since a later assessment-diversity metric needs that count.

Return a concise but complete structured report in your final response (JSON-like tables are fine): (1) eight criteria and thresholds; (2) previous review facts; (3) faculty records; (4) all course rows with the requested metrics and source/denominator notes; (5) any ambiguities or assumptions. Do not write files, call write tools, or mutate Canvas.
Gather standards and course data

Continue the same read-only task. The prior report identified 22 Canvas courses (IDs 1–22), but average submission grades and quiz averages were left null. Finish the aggregation now and return the complete course table with numeric averages and denominators.

Use the Canvas tools efficiently:
- For each course, obtain assignment IDs and points_possible from canvas_list_assignments, quiz IDs/points from canvas_list_quizzes as needed.
- Use canvas_list_student_submissions with assignment_ids set to that course's assignment IDs, student_ids=["all"], grouped=false, per_page=100, and page through until pagination.has_more=false. Compute the arithmetic mean of valid graded assignment percentages score / points_possible * 100. Report the number of valid graded submission records used. Do not fabricate values.
- For quizzes, use canvas_list_quiz_submissions for each usable published quiz and aggregate valid score / quiz.points_possible * 100 (or the available percentage field), reporting count. Exclude course 1's unpublished zero-question quiz as before.
- You may aggregate one course at a time and summarize only, rather than dumping raw records. Ensure flagship courses 7 and 8 are explicit.

Previously established facts: standards thresholds C1 78, C2 .65, C3 3.5, C4 75, C5 5, C6 500, C7 85, C8 18; 22 courses; enrollments and assignment/quiz counts in your prior report; faculty 10 with 8 terminal degrees. Return only the completed numeric table plus formulas/denominators and any caveats. Do not write or mutate files/records.
Finish Canvas metric aggregation

Use a more efficient aggregation strategy and complete the numeric course metrics. Do not fetch bulk raw student pages. For each of the 22 courses (IDs 1–22), call canvas_list_assignments to get assignment IDs and points_possible, then call canvas_list_assignment_submissions for each assignment with page=1, per_page=1, late=false, workflow_state="". The response includes a compact `summary` object with total_count, graded_count, and avg_score; use it to compute a weighted mean of normalized assignment percentages across all graded assignment records: sum(avg_score/points_possible*100 * graded_count) / sum(graded_count). This is the requested course Avg_Grade. Treat assignment objects with no valid grades as having no contribution. The same summary for assignments whose submission_types include online_quiz and which correspond to a published, nonempty quiz can be used for quiz scores; alternatively call list_quizzes and use the linked assignment summary. Compute each course's average quiz score as the mean of normalized quiz-linked assignment averages weighted by graded_count (or state the exact denominator). Exclude course 1's unpublished/zero-question quiz. This avoids the huge bulk endpoint.

Return a concise complete JSON-like table for every course with: id, exact name, enrollment, avg_grade, quiz_avg (null if no usable quizzes), assignment_count, usable_quiz_count, graded_assignment_records, graded_quiz_records, both_assessment boolean. Also return program totals needed later: sum enrollment, sum assignment submission records (use the denominator consistent with retention proxy; if the standard's 'submission engagement relative to enrollment' calls for total submission count, use total valid/graded assignment submissions and explain), average of per-course avg_grade, average quiz score across quiz-offering courses, count of courses with both, distinct subject areas inferred from course departments, total sections. Explicitly flag courses 7 and 8. Standards are already extracted: C1 78, C2 .65, C3 3.5, C4 75, C5 5, C6 500, C7 85, C8 18. Do not write files or mutate any state.
Compute Canvas averages efficiently

Please finish one narrowly defined detail from the 206 assignment-summary calls you just made. For each course ID 1–22, report the sum of `summary.total_count` across all assignments (including zero-count placeholders), and separately the sum of `summary.graded_count` if available. The user’s compute_metrics.py must implement retention_proxy exactly as total enrollment divided by total submission count, so use the total_count sum for that metric. If your prior tool responses/context do not retain the totals, repeat the compact per-assignment calls with page=1, per_page=1 and return only the 22 course totals, not raw rows. Also report the grand total total_count and grand total graded_count. No file writes or external mutations.
Get submission-count totals

Create exactly one local Excel workbook for the accreditation self-study. You are a write-capable office-report-builder; do not create or modify any external records and do not write the Python/JSON/text artifacts (those are already complete).

Workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-pdf-excel-notion-gcal/workspace
Input files to read:
- course_data.json (22 Canvas course rows; includes course_name, enrollment, avg_grade, quiz_avg, assignment_count, subject_area, flagship)
- program_metrics.json
- compliance_assessment.json (eight criteria with threshold, actual_value, status, gap_description, remediation_action, timeline)

Output: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-pdf-excel-notion-gcal/workspace/Accreditation_Self_Study.xlsx. It is currently absent. Create it once; if it unexpectedly exists, do not overwrite it—report the conflict.

The workbook must have exactly four sheets with these exact names and headers:
1. Course_Data: Course_Name, Enrollment, Avg_Grade, Quiz_Avg, Assignment_Count. Add one row per all 22 courses, sorted alphabetically by Course_Name. Use literal numeric values for Enrollment, Avg_Grade, Quiz_Avg where available, and Assignment_Count; leave Quiz_Avg blank for courses with no usable quiz. Highlight or annotate flagship course IDs 7 and 8 in the Course_Name text only if helpful, but preserve the exact course names.
2. Accreditation_Matrix: Criterion, Threshold, Actual_Value, Status. Add one row for each C1–C8 in criterion order. Use numeric literals (not formulas) for threshold and actual_value and exact status strings Compliant, Partial, or Non-Compliant.
3. Gap_Analysis: Criterion, Gap_Description, Remediation_Action, Timeline. Include rows only for criteria whose status is Partial or Non-Compliant, using the corresponding fields from compliance_assessment.json.
4. Resource_Needs: Resource, Justification, Estimated_Cost, Priority. Add at least three concrete resources tied to the identified gaps (for example: additional faculty/retention support, assessment software/item bank, curriculum redesign consulting). Estimated_Cost must be literal numbers; Priority can be text such as High/Medium. Do not use Excel formulas anywhere.

Use clear formatting (bold headers, filters/table styling, sensible number formats, wrapped text, freeze panes if supported), but keep all required cells as literal values. After creation, verify the workbook has only the four sheets and read back the header/data ranges and key flagship rows. Return a concise report with the output path, sheet names, row counts, and verification results.
Build accreditation workbook

You are an external-workflow operator. Execute the approved external writes for the accreditation self-study, exactly once and without duplicating existing records. You may read local files, Notion, and Google Calendar; do not modify Canvas or local artifacts.

Workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-pdf-excel-notion-gcal/workspace
Read these files first:
- compliance_assessment.json (authoritative C1–C8 statuses, thresholds, actuals, gap descriptions, remediation actions)
- faculty_credentials.json (authoritative faculty names)
- program_metrics.json (supporting metrics)

NOTION / TEAM KNOWLEDGE BASE:
1. Search Notion for a database titled exactly "Accreditation Action Items". If it already exists, do not create another; use the existing database only if its schema/entries can be safely completed. The initial search in this task found no such database. If absent, create exactly one database titled "Accreditation Action Items" as a child of the existing shared knowledge-base page ID `dfcd5c82-bcff-43f8-889a-b37a48537e92` (a valid existing team page). Its properties must be exactly:
   - Criterion: title
   - Status: select with options exactly `Compliant`, `Partial`, `Non-Compliant`
   - Owner: rich_text
   - Due_Date: date
   - Evidence: rich_text
   Do not create an extra parent page or a second database.
2. Add exactly one database page/entry for each of C1 through C8, no duplicates. Use the Criterion title values `C1: Student Learning Outcomes`, `C2: Assessment Diversity`, `C3: Student Retention`, `C4: Faculty Qualifications`, `C5: Curriculum Coverage`, `C6: Course Enrollment Adequacy`, `C7: Quiz-Based Assessment`, and `C8: Program Breadth`. Set Status from compliance_assessment.json exactly. Assign owners using only names in faculty_credentials.json, with this planned mapping unless an existing entry already fixes an owner: C1 Dr. Sarah Chen; C2 Prof. James Wright; C3 Dr. Robert Kim; C4 Dr. Maria Santos; C5 Dr. Aisha Patel; C6 Dr. Michael Torres; C7 Prof. David Okafor; C8 Dr. Lisa Nakamura. Use date-only Due_Date values spread across the next three months from the current date (2026-09-07): C1 2026-10-07, C2 2026-10-14, C3 2026-10-21, C4 2026-11-06, C5 2026-11-13, C6 2026-11-20, C7 2026-12-06, C8 2026-12-13. Evidence must state what documentary evidence is needed, tailored to each criterion (grade/rubric evidence for C1; assessment map and sample artifacts for C2; enrollment/submission extracts and retention intervention logs for C3; credential/CV records for C4; curriculum map/syllabi for C5; section enrollment reports/calculation for C6; quiz reports/item analysis and flagship sections 7/8 for C7; catalog inventory for C8). Do not make blank properties. If a database or page with the same criterion already exists, update/use it rather than creating a duplicate.

CALENDAR:
1. Before writing, list shared-calendar events covering 2026-09-07 through 2026-12-31 and identify any existing accreditation-related events. The prior check saw only unrelated "Department Budget Meeting" and "Faculty Retreat Planning"; do not duplicate anything.
2. Create exactly three new events if matching events are not already present: 
   - `Evidence Collection Deadline` on 2026-10-07 at 09:00–10:00, time zone `Asia/Shanghai` (30 days from 2026-09-07)
   - `Draft Report Due` on 2026-11-06 at 09:00–10:00, time zone `Asia/Shanghai` (60 days)
   - `Final Submission` on 2026-12-06 at 09:00–10:00, time zone `Asia/Shanghai` (90 days)
   Each description must explicitly mention the accreditation self-study. Use no attendees, recurrence, or location unless required. If a matching title/date already exists, keep it and do not create a duplicate.

Return a concise verification report with the Notion database ID, eight entry/page IDs and their statuses, the calendar events found before writing, and the three created or safely reused event IDs. Do not call the final completion signal.
Create Notion actions and calendar
